title: A Quieter Boat Propeller Could Help Whales Hear Each Other
summary:
A Detroit company called Sharrow Marine is working with Ocean Alliance, a marine conservation organization, to test quieter boat propellers on research trips near whales. The tests are still at an early stage.

Noise pollution happens underwater as well as on busy streets. Large ships and other human-made machines add sound to the ocean. When the ocean is quiet, whales can hear each other's calls from hundreds of miles away. They use these calls to communicate and find food. Noise from shipping overlaps with the low sounds whales use, making their calls harder to hear.

Much of a boat's noise comes from its propeller, the spinning part that pushes it through water. A process called cavitation happens when tiny bubbles form behind a fast-spinning propeller. When the bubbles pop, they make hissing or crackling sounds.

Instead of blades with separate tips, Sharrow's design uses looped blades that twist like a ribbon. The company says this shape reduces cavitation. It claims independent testing found underwater noise reductions of up to seven decibels in the sound range whales use to communicate. Decibels are units used to measure sound levels. The company says results vary with operating conditions.

The idea began with a different problem. Greg Sharrow, the company's founder and CEO, wanted to film a violinist inside an orchestra using a camera drone. The drone's buzzing would interfere with the music. He began thinking about a propeller without separate blade tips, then realized the idea could also work on boats. His early boat propeller tests took place in a fish tank.

Ocean Alliance CEO Iain Kerr supports solutions that benefit animals, the environment and boat users. The research trips will explore the quieter design near whales. Whether it meaningfully improves whales' ability to hear one another remains an open question.
why_it_matters: Whales depend on hearing calls. Testing quieter boat parts could help researchers explore ways to reduce noise that interferes with those calls.
